caveats: Reported line values are bootstrap means; errors are the bootstrap standard deviation (upstream PyQSOFitSpec convention), not a covariance matrix.
53 valid bootstrap realisations were used (requested 55); the uncertainty of the uncertainty is ~10 %.
Ugriz-type flux calibration slippage and Fe II template systematics dominate over the statistical error; the bootstrap captures neither.

PyQSOFitSpec fits a single skewed profile per listed component; the Mg II 2796/2804 doublet is a single blended component, and the [O III] 5007 total is core + broad wing (and, if present, any intermediate component listed in line_definitions).
The broad/narrow label is the component's declared kind from the config (kind field), not the fitted width; QSOFit.line_prop still uses its 0.0017 log10(sigma) cut internally to select profiles.

The H-beta total is Hb_br+Hb_na.  It is larger than GANDALF/S3Fit because PyQSOFitSpec fits one skew-normal broad component on a different Fe II continuum; the data-minus-continuum integral in 4640-4940 A is ~10-20 % larger with this continuum.  The offset is a model/continuum definition difference, not a units error.
The optical table has no separate He II 4687 component: He II 4687 is absorbed by Hb_br.  PyQSOFit fits HeII4687_br/_na explicitly, so its H-beta broad flux is not defined identically.
Widths fixed by configuration (NLR anchor) for MgII_na, OIII5007c: their fluxes are measured, but their widths are not fitted parameters (see line_definitions.nlr_width_anchor).
Widths and velocities tied to OIII5007c for Hb_na, OIII4959c; they are not independent measurements.
Widths and velocities tied to OIII5007w for OIII4959w; they are not independent measurements.
unstable/multimodal components (16-84 interval > 25% of the mean): OIII4959c, OIII5007c, OIII4959w, OIII5007w; use the summed totals in pyqsofitspec_totals.csv for line-ratio work.

The QSO model has no host-galaxy/stellar SSP term; the AGN continuum is powerlaw + Fe II + Balmer continuum + SKIRTOR torus.
The SKIRTOR torus is constrained by the four WISE bands only (no far-IR/mm data).

The input spectrum is scaled to the SDSS griz photometry before the joint fit; line fluxes are in that calibrated normalization. Divide by fit.spec_calib_ratio for the raw-SDSS comparison used by PyQSOFit/GANDALF/GalSpec/QGfit.
Mg II 2796/2804 is fitted as a tied doublet (ratio 1.0, S3Fit's atomic ratio) because the two broad components are blended and individually degenerate.
Lines whose rest-frame centres fall outside the fitted spectrum are removed before fitting; see scope.line_coverage and line_list_note.

Runtime compromise (model grid unchanged, 10 mocks retained): dual-annealing global search disabled (if_run_init_annealing=false); nlfit_ntry_max=1 (reference default 3); accept_chi_sq=10.0 to avoid repeated recycle fits.

entries.caveat: Uses official XMM PPS products, not a raw SAS epproc/especget reduction. Fe K-alpha is 4.05 sigma; PN/MOS Gamma differ by 2.9 sigma; the broad Fe width is degenerate with continuum curvature and is not a resolved velocity.
caveats: PPS official products; SAS epproc/especget/specgroup were not run.
MOS 5 eV PPS spectra rebinned 3:1 to 15 eV for the 15 eV canned RMF named in the PPS header.
PN RMF is CCF v22.0; PPS products were generated with SAS 21.0.0 (2024).
RMF FILTER=Medium vs observation Thin1 is expected; the ARF carries the filter throughput.
tbabs*zpowerlw leaves chi2/dof ~1.70; soft excess and reflection are not modeled.
The free-width Fe K-alpha Gaussian is degenerate with continuum curvature; the primary narrow-core width is fixed to 50 eV.
The free-centroid fit gives E_rest ~ 6.18 keV; the single Gaussian captures a redshifted/broad Fe complex.
PN and MOS Gamma differ by 2.9 sigma (MOS1), a cross-calibration systematic.
Errors are XSPEC covariance 1-sigma; no MCMC.
